notes: kuna-fixes cases: classes Vineflower 1.12.0 fails on that a kuna fix decompiles. Each runs in compat and in default mode on the fixture's base map plus `options`; maintained by tests/jvm/kuna_fix_case.py, read by regen.py.

cases.summary: `objects` and `shapes`, which pass `factory::create` on a `Factory<?>`/`ShapeFactory<?>` receiver to a generic `map`, decompile to their source; the failure comments and bytecode listings are gone
`create` and `attempt`, whose `catch (Throwable)` handlers start with `if (!flag)`, decompile to their source; `read`, a try-with-resources on a nullable resource, is still rebuilt as one

`assertThenTryFinally` decompiles; `tryFinallyThenCode` and `tryCatchReturn` keep the code after the if on the path through the try (Vineflower skips it with a `break`), and `tryFinallyThenReturn` keeps its source shape; the recompiled class's `javap -c -p` equals the original's

the eight methods whose switch expression yields a string or class literal next to an arm of another reference type (a boxed char, int or boolean, a StringBuilder, a Class), as an argument, a returned value, a local and inside a lambda, decompile to their source; the failure comments and bytecode listings are gone

`read`, `readThree`, `readOrDefault`, `readGuarded` and `readFinally` (a `while (true)` after other code around a `try` whose two or three `catch` blocks all go back to the loop) decompile to their source, `readOrDefault`'s `break` as `return -1` in its `catch` block, the way Vineflower prints such a `break`; the failure comments and bytecode listings are gone

`iterator`, whose `object : Iterator<String>` captures the extension receiver and gets the parameterless `remove()` stub kotlinc adds, decompiles; `remove()` is written as a plain method instead of being taken for an extension of the captured receiver

`byLength`, `byLengthOf` (which creates `byLength`'s object), `nullsFirstBy` (two early `return@Comparator`s) and `twice` (a `crossinline` function-type lambda) decompile to `object` expressions whose methods return what the source returns; the failure comments are gone
`make`, whose object has a function and an inner class with a default computed by an inlined `map`, decompiles; those defaults print as unknown (`= ...`), the simple one as `n: Int = 7`

`twoDefaults` and `oneDefault`, whose objects' inner classes call the superclass through its default-arguments constructor, decompile with `: TestDefaultArgsSuperCall(x)` and `(x, y)`; `otherConstructor` still fails by design: `Overloaded` has a one-argument secondary constructor that `Overloaded(x)` would call

`sweep`, `lastOfHead`, `firstOf`, `itemLength` and `lengthOf`, which use a `Node` nested in the non-generic inner class `Itrs` of the generic class, decompile to their source, `E` mapped to `String` through `Itrs` where the instance is a `TestInnerOfGenericOuter<String>` one; the failure comments and bytecode listings are gone

the class, whose synthetic `body` creates the lambda it implements (as the constructor does), decompiles: both sites are written as `this::body`, and `body` stays a method (left out here, as every synthetic method is under `remove-synthetic`); `plain`'s ordinary lambda is still written in place

every `new DiamondLib(..)`/`new DiamondBox()` whose expected type is a `DiamondLib<..>`/`DiamondBox<..>` (static and instance fields, a local, returns, an assignment, arguments, a ternary operand, a generic class's field) is written `new C<>(..)`, so the lambdas get their `Object[]` parameters back and the class recompiles to identical bytecode; `Object OBJECT = new DiamondBox()` and the non-generic `DiamondPlain` stay as they are

`consistent`, `noFailure`, `unreachable` and `plain`, whose lambdas are a lone `assert`, get block bodies; `drain`, whose inner loop ends with an `assert`, stays a `while` loop with the `assert` at the end of its body; Vineflower prints both in expression positions, which javac rejects

the inner anonymous class's call of its enclosing anonymous class's static `twice` is written `twice(value)`, not `<unrepresentable>.twice(value)`; the call of a named class's static method keeps its qualifier

the dead `throw new AssertionError(...)` statements after `return` in `spans` and `widths` are gone, and `widths` declares its for-each variable in the header (`for (int[] row : rows)`, was `for (row : rows)`)
the enums without constants, `TestEnumNoConstants` and `Only`, start their bodies with the `;` Java requires before members; `Empty` (no members) is unchanged

`once`, `twice` and `early`, suspend functions whose try/finally spans a suspension point, decompile: the try of the tail keeps its inlined finally and each range part the exception deobfuscator split off becomes a try/finally guarded by a semaphore variable

`describe`, two record deconstruction patterns inside a try/catch, decompiles to its source (one try, the second pattern in a conditional expression); recompiled with javac its bytecode equals the original's

`drain` (a suspend loop inside try/catch/finally) and `first` decompile; the loop body irreducible-flow splitting copies for the resume path keeps its finally, guarded by the same semaphore variable (with the fixes handler_copy_offsets and nested_handler_copies)
case Kind.CIRCLE beside type patterns in a switch on an interface: the enum label is resolved and printed qualified

cases with several labels (case Integer _, String _; case Kind.CIRCLE, Kind.SQUARE; case 5, 7) and an integer label equal to a later switch index: every label is resolved, multi-pattern cases print as one unnamed-pattern label
case 42 beside case Integer i when ... on an Integer, String or Character selector (no checkcast, no LocalVariableTable): the pattern is typed by its class, the selector keeps its type
a @JvmOverloads overload and the function of an object written inside a lambda return their values (Vineflower prints the values as bare expression statements)
a DefaultImpls method whose body fails is printed with its failure comment (Vineflower leaves it out of the class without a trace)
an object expression's superclass is written with its constructor arguments, object : Base(k + 1, s) (Vineflower prints object : Base)

the primary constructor's `Array<String>` parameter is no longer written `vararg names: Any`, and the `vararg` primitive parameters of a constructor and a function keep `vararg` with their element type (`vararg rest: Int`, not `rest: IntArray`)

`chain` and `twice`, whose defaults are computed through locals, print the unknown default `= ...` instead of the first local's initializer `this.measure(s)`; `plain` keeps `b: Int = this.measure(a) + 1`
the constructor calls whose type arguments Kotlin infers (`return Bag(0)`, `Pair(a, b)`) are written without the Java diamond `<>`

the local class written inside the object is one indented line, `/* $VF: local visibility outside of method */ internal inner class Sub : ...`, instead of a line comment naming `methodSupplier` followed by the header at column 0
the inner class `Sink` declares its defaults (`finished: Boolean = false, limit: Long = 16L`) instead of the unknown `= ...`

`skipsMiddle` (`TestDefaultArgsSuperNamed(a = x, c = 9L)`), `innerSuper` (an inner superclass, `Inner(z)`) and `picksPrimary` (`Overloaded(a = x)`, named because `Overloaded(x)` would select the secondary constructor) decompile; `picksSecondary` keeps `Overloaded(x)`

`sum` and `fold`, suspend loops: the result of the suspend call is cast to `Integer` after the `COROUTINE_SUSPENDED` check, as in the bytecode, not before it (where the marker would throw `ClassCastException`)

`intOrLong`, `charOrInt` and `argument`, whose switch expressions yield numbers of different types to a reference target: the switch is no longer wrapped in a cast, which made it a standalone numeric switch (`case 1 -> 1` a `Long`)

the conditionals whose boxed arms would print as numbers of different types (`int` and `long`, `int` and `Integer`, `boolean` and `Boolean`, `Double` and `double`) keep an arm cast, so they stay reference conditionals: no promotion of `1` to `Long`, no unboxing of a `null` arm
`firstLength`, whose two block-scoped locals share a slot: the `Object` one is no longer merged into the `String` one, so `src.next()` is not cast to `String` before it is compared with `MARK`

`bound` and `boundMutable` (`box::size`, `box::count`, which failed) and `member`, `mutableMember`, `topLevel` and `extension` (whose singleton `INSTANCE`s printed `<unrepresentable>.INSTANCE`) write their property references `Box::size`, `Box::count`, `::answer`, `Box::doubled`

`bound` (`adder::add`, which failed) and `unbound`, `constructor` and `topLevel` (whose singleton `INSTANCE`s printed `<unrepresentable>.INSTANCE`) write their function references: `NestedClassProcessor` took the reference classes' `super(..)` calls out of their constructors, and they are read from the class node
the local class is declared before new LocalClass<String>() {} instead of inside the later loop that uses LocalClass.class

cases.compiler: javac 17.0.20.1 (`-g`, against a `lib.Base` that is not in the input)
cases.summary: protected member classes of a library class used in a subclass (Base.Helper, Base.Holder.Deep, an enum switched on, one inside an anonymous subclass) are written Base.Helper, not imported

cases.compiler: javac 17.0.20.1 (`-g`) (with ext/TestOverrideInaccessibleBase.java, vendored as a second input class)
cases.summary: methods matching a package-private superclass method of another package or a private one get no @Override; true overrides keep it
a local assigned on the other path of the instanceof, or read after the if, keeps its declaration and cast; a local used only inside the branch still becomes a pattern
two cases declaring double z before an if, and a case-level int length clashing with a nested one in a later case, are written with braces
Source<? extends byte[]> and Source<? super int[]> keep their wildcards, so BytesEncoder.encode overrides Encoder<byte[]>.encode

`sumBackwards` and `total`, whose `for` loops the plugin cannot resugar, are written `while (i >= 0)` and `while (node != null)` instead of `while (true) { if (COND) break`, which leaves each loop at once

`weighted` (bound assigned before the counter), `skipping` (counter assigned in the body) and `sumUntilBig` (condition on another variable) are written as `while` loops instead of the ranges `for (n in a.length..i)`, `repeat(limit) { var5 ->` and `repeat(99) { i ->`
`for (i in from until to)` and `repeat(10)` instead of the off-by-one `for (i in from..to)` and `repeat(9)`
the loop `while (i < a.length)`, which Vineflower leaves out (its bound is neither a constant nor a variable), is written
the counter of the loop written as a `while` is declared, `var var4: Int`, before the loop

the loop whose body continues it is written `if (i < limit) { label35@ do { ... } while (run { i++; i < limit }) }`, so `continue@label35` runs `i++`, instead of an inclusive range over a counter the body assigns
the two elvis results keep their own variables, `return if (var10000.size > var9.size) var10000 else var9`, instead of one variable that the second overwrites (`var10000.size > var10000.size`)
`rows`, `grid` and `table`, which create an array of arrays with only its outer length, decompile (`arrayOfNulls(n)`)

`run` and `poll`, loops entered at their head and, from a resume branch, in their middle, whose body is protected by one catch-all in several ranges with an unprotected early `return` between them, decompile; the try is built inside its own region or a statement outside every range is copied, and the output recompiles and behaves as the original on 140,000 scripted runs (`run` fails earlier in Vineflower, IndexOutOfBounds, the fix `handler_copy_offsets`)

`indexOf`, `pairs` and `watch`, suspend functions whose loop inside a `try` (with `catch`/`finally`) suspends and resumes in its middle, decompile: `indexOf` and `pairs` once a try region is isolated or a statement outside every range is copied, `watch` (whose loop is resumed in three places) with both

the stores to each finally semaphore are kept, `var var8: Boolean = false /* VF: Semaphore variable */`, `var8 = true` at the try's entry and `var8 = false` on every normal exit, instead of a guard `if (var8)` that reads a variable declared after it (`val var8: Boolean`, `val var13: <unknown>`) while `true` goes to another variable

asserts at the end of a loop body and before a return, which the structurer wrote as if ($assertionsDisabled || cond) { rest } throw new AssertionError(), are resugared; no $assertionsDisabled reference is left
catch variables of lambda bodies renamed for a clash with the enclosing method (e -> ex, ex -> exx/exxx) are declared under the name their uses read
an anonymous class's method parameter e, whose uses are written e, is declared e instead of ex (the name the rename for a captured variable whose slot the enclosing catch variable e reuses gave it)
a top-level sealed class whose permitted subclasses are its private members is written without the permits clause javac rejects; a nested sealed class and one permitting public records keep theirs

switch statements that assign a local more than once in a case, leave a case through an if without else or a loop exit, or have an empty case stay switch statements instead of switch expressions with unreachable or missing yields
a switch-expression arm declaring internalName inside a case of a switch statement whose earlier case declares internalName gets that case in braces instead of a duplicate declaration
type annotations on a later generic argument (Fn<Pair<String, @A Object>, @A Pair<String, @A Object>>) are written in that argument, not repeated in an earlier one

cases.compiler: javac 17.0.20.1 (`-g`, against a `lib.AnnotatedHolder` that is not in the input)
cases.summary: type-annotated uses of lib.AnnotatedHolder.Entry, which the class's own nested Entry shadows, keep their qualifier (lib.AnnotatedHolder.@A Entry) instead of naming the nested class
the casts to the type variables `T` and `N` keep their boxing calls (`(T)Integer.valueOf(0)`), as Java has no cast from a primitive to a type variable; `(Object)` still boxes implicitly

the calls to the inner classes' `sub`, `remove` and `put` pass their arguments without the casts to the neighbouring parameter's type (`(boolean)from`, `(V)key`, `(long)value`) that javac rejects; the `(K)` cast an unresolved argument needs stays

the lambdas and the method reference passed where two overloads take different functional interfaces of the same shape keep the cast to their interface (`(IntSink)this::add`) that picks the overload; the call with one overload stays without a cast
`toArray` on a raw `Bag` keeps the `(String[])` cast its erased `Object[]` result needs, and the for-each loops over a raw `Bag` cast it to `Bag<String>` so that the `String` loop variable compiles
the static `value` passes its `ListenableBox<?>` without a cast to `Box<V>`, whose `V` is the class's type variable and not in scope in a static method

the values returned or assigned where their declared generic type does not fit (`NullEntry.INSTANCE` as an `Entry<K, V>`, `this` as a `TestUncheckedGenericCast<K1, V1>`, a `? super K` ordering as an `Ordering<Object>`) keep the unchecked casts the bytecode cannot show; `order()`, whose value fits, gets none

the `instanceof` tests whose cast is unchecked (`List<String>` from an `Object`, `Pair<String, Integer>` from a `Box<String>`, a type variable) keep the `instanceof` and the cast instead of becoming type patterns javac rejects; `Leaf<String>` from a `Box<String>` and `List<?>` stay patterns
the labels of the `when` over `name.hashCode()` are the hash codes, `45679 ->`, where Vineflower writes them as characters, `'뉯' ->`

the `@JvmOverloads` overload of `describe`, which returns `Object`, is written `fun describe(value: Any?): Any?` with its `return`, where Vineflower writes it without a return type and drops the `return` (and `pick`'s overload gets its `return`)
each bodiless secondary constructor ends its line, so `Base`'s last one is followed by the class's closing brace on the next line, where Vineflower writes `: this(0)   }`
`allDigits`'s loop is `for (index in (if (..) 1 else 0) until length)`, where Vineflower leaves the `if` bare, which makes the range its `else` branch

`search`'s lambda, whose `return@search i` is inside its loop, is labelled and returns with `return@lambda_1 i`, where Vineflower writes the bare `i`, so the loop goes on and the lambda returns `-1`; `clamp`, `firstNegative` and `sign`, whose results are in tail position, are unchanged

the class's type parameters are named in its members' types and in the inner class `Cursor`'s (`fun key(i: Int): K`, `keys: Array<K>`, `fun advance(step: V): Pair<K, V>`), where Vineflower writes `Any` for each

numeric conversions are Kotlin's conversion calls, `l.toInt()`, `d.toInt().toByte()`, `Math.min(byteCount, (8192 - limit).toLong()).toInt()`, and casts to a type variable `as` casts, `this.items[i] as T`, where Vineflower writes Java's casts, `(int)l`, `(byte)d`, `(T)this.items[i]`
qualifier calls whose type variables only lambdas or inexact method references fix get explicit type arguments; recompiles to the original bytecode
a lambda passed for a bare type variable that javac resolves from the other arguments to another type is cast to its interface; recompiles to the original bytecode
a returned call whose declared result does not fit the target keeps its unchecked cast (to the raw class where the result's type argument is a type variable); recompiles to the original bytecode

`labelled`, whose `continue outer` leaves an inner loop that is the outer loop's last statement, keeps its exit (`break;`); Vineflower prints none, so the inner loop runs on (`labelled({3, 1, 2})` returns 0 instead of 6); `whileTrue` and `doWhile` are unchanged

the inner class's generic methods, whose `<T>` shadows the class's `<T extends Number>`, keep their `(Number)` casts; Vineflower drops them, so `pick` calls `use(Object)` instead of `use(Number)` and `widen` does not compile; `method` is unchanged
`lowestBit`, whose `int` shift count `sz` shifts a `long` with `>>>=`, compares `sz != 0`; Vineflower types `sz` as a `long` there and prints `sz != false`; `rotate` is unchanged

the dead stores `override = 0` and `last = 1`, split into variables of their own and declared `int` from the local variable table, are initialized with `0` and `1`; Vineflower prints `int var4 = false;` and `int var7 = true;`
`invoke`, whose `try` body always returns, keeps `this.log(ex)` in its catch clause; Vineflower moves it after the `try`, out of the scope of `ex`; `first` and `retry` are unchanged

`build`, which assigns `new BaseSupplier<V0>(key)` through a raw cast to a `Supplier<Box<V>>`, writes the `new` raw; Vineflower writes a diamond javac cannot infer (`Key<V0>` against `Box<V>`); `direct` keeps its diamond

calls through the default-arguments bridges (`join$default(base, 0, null, 6, null)`, `scale$default(other, ..)`, `Shape.DefaultImpls.area$default(s, 0, 1, null)`, `Box(base, 0, null, 6, null)`) are written as the source's calls (`join(this.base)`, `other.scale(y = true)`, `s.area()`, `Box(w = this.base, tag = "t")`); the class recompiled from them has the original's bytecode

the no-argument constructor kotlinc adds for `TestGeneratedConstructors`'s all-default parameters and `Overloads`' two `@JvmOverloads` constructors are no longer written as functions (`fun Overloads(a: Int) { this(a, 0L, false, 6, null) }`); the delegation `this(s.length(), 0, 2, null)` reads `this(a = s.length())` (`kt_default_args_call`); recompiled, the three classes have the original's bytecode

the casts Vineflower writes in Java's syntax are Kotlin's: `values as Array<V>?` (a parameter declared nullable), `null as String?`, `arrayOfNulls(size) as Array<T>`, `one(element) as Box<T>`, and `32.toLong()` for `(long)32`
`lastLabel`'s call is `Seqs.lastOf<Item>(items)`, where Vineflower writes Java's `Seqs.<Item>lastOf(items)`

`overriding`, whose local is reassigned `mods = new LinkedMods(mods)` under one LocalVariableTable entry, stays one `Mods` variable (the merge is widened to the declared type rather than refused); `firstLength`, whose two block-scoped locals have their own entries, still keeps two variables, so `src.next()` is not stored in an `Object` that is then used as a `String`

`boundMangled` (`h::mark`, which failed) and `unboundMangled` (whose singleton printed `<unrepresentable>.INSTANCE`) write their references to `mark`, a function with an inline-class parameter whose JVM name is mangled (`mark-1pYyLzM`): the signature constant is split at its `(`, not after the Kotlin name
an abstract class's constructors are its primary constructor (header and init), and a secondary constructor, not functions named after the class
a constructor's code after its super/this call that starts with an if is written (init block, secondary constructor body), not dropped
a constructor with an inline-class parameter is read from its real private constructor: the header calls the real supertype, no function named after the class
a jump out of a labelled if is return@label from run label@{ .. }, the next iteration of a repeat loop return@label, not break/continue to a label that is not a loop's

cases.compiler: kotlinc 2.0.0 (-jvm-target 17); kotlin.Metadata d1 then edited to drop the constructor signature's desc, the shape kotlin-stdlib 2.2.20's kotlin/Unit.class has
cases.summary: an object's constructor whose metadata has no JVM descriptor is found by the descriptor its parameters give, not written as a function
a multifile class part's constructor (kotlinc -Xmultifile-parts-inherit) is not written as a top-level open fun named after the part

a break out of a when is left out where its branch ends after it (string when, nested when) and is return@labelN from a run labelN@{ .. } around the when otherwise, not break, which Kotlin rejects outside a loop
a jump at the end of a try block with a finally is written in Kotlin's syntax (break, then left out where it ends a when branch), not Java's break;
a catch block that ends in continue or break keeps the jump, which Vineflower drops (the catch path then fell through to code reading the try's unassigned result)
